blocks.text: Isaiah 23 belongs to a wider sequence in which Isaiah speaks judgment not only against Judah and Israel but also against foreign nations. Across the book, powerful empires can serve a purpose yet remain accountable themselves, while nations are also envisioned as learning, worshiping, and sharing in restoration. The text of Isaiah has been actively transmitted and interpreted: the Great Isaiah Scroll preserves an almost complete form of the book broadly aligned with the Masoretic tradition, though it contains many spelling and substantive differences, alongside other Isaiah manuscripts and interpretations from Qumran.
